label: One admissible profile has one favouring, good-general if it has good-generality
paraphrase: OPEN analyst bridge, attribution deferred: every admissible intrinsic profile q (a set of real determinations a simple, unreceived, necessary source could jointly have) is realized by one favouring profile psi: every favouring determination in q is the determination that a favouring of the bearer is psi, and if q contains the good-generality determination, psi is good-general (for some scenario and candidates, at least one not a present input, it depends on betterness, read as value, with end-realization held fixed, BECAUSE_OF_GOODNESS_2). That an admissible profile has at most one favouring is an open reading of what a simple source's favouring is; it is not derived from the encoded simplicity of #2153 (no represented limiting principle), which a root with two favourings can keep, and a simple root may carry several other distinct determinations. It is a reading of the favouring tokens and of admissibility, not a theorem about them.
